items.title: AlertDialog button with null listener throws NullPointerException on click
items.android_behavior: AOSP lets the listener be null: setNegativeButton("Cancel", null) is the standard idiom, and clicking just dismisses the dialog.
items.impact: Clicking any button registered with a null listener (very common Cancel/OK buttons) crashes the app with an NPE instead of closing the dialog.
items.suggested_fix: if (listener != null) listener.onClick(AlertDialog.this, whichButton); dismiss();
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/app/AlertDialog.java, method setButton(int whichButton, CharSequence text, OnClickListener listener): inside the anonymous View.OnClickListener.onClick, change `listener.onClick(AlertDialog.this, whichButton);` to `if (listener != null) listener.onClick(AlertDialog.this, whichButton);`. Keep the following `dismiss();` unconditional (AOSP AlertController dismisses the dialog after any button click, even when the listener is null). Change nothing else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: setButton wraps the listener without a null check, so setPositiveButton(text, null) throws an NPE on click. The fix is a one-line Java null guard, and AOSP behaviour is clear: a button with a null listener still dismisses the dialog.

items.title: setPaddingRelative() is empty, so padding set from code with start/end is dropped
items.evidence: public void setPaddingRelative(int start, int top, int end, int bottom) {}
items.android_behavior: AOSP sets start/top/end/bottom padding, resolved to left/right in LTR. ViewCompat.setPaddingRelative() calls it directly on API 17+. AppCompat, Material components (Chip, MaterialButton, TextInputLayout, Toolbar), RecyclerView item decorations and many apps call it.
items.impact: Views padded from code have no padding: text touches edges, icons overlap labels and list items are cramped. getPaddingStart() still returns the old value, so later measurement math is also wrong.
items.suggested_fix: Implement it as setPadding(start, top, end, bottom) for LTR, or swap start and end when getLayoutDirection() is RTL.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/View.java, make setPaddingRelative(int start, int top, int end, int bottom) call setPadding(start, top, end, bottom). This ATL View is always LTR (getLayoutDirection() returns LAYOUT_DIRECTION_LTR, and getPaddingStart() returns paddingLeft), so start maps to left and end maps to right. Do not touch anything else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: the method is empty (View.java:2307). getLayoutDirection() always returns LTR and getPaddingStart/End already map to left/right, so the fix is one line forwarding to setPadding.

items.title: setImageBitmap and setImageResource (bitmap path) never update the drawable field, so getDrawable() is stale or null and the tint is lost
items.android_behavior: Both methods wrap the image in a BitmapDrawable and go through updateDrawable, so getDrawable() returns it, the ImageView's tint and colour filter apply, and the old drawable's callback is cleared.
items.impact: ((BitmapDrawable)iv.getDrawable()).getBitmap() returns null or the previous image, which causes crashes or wrong shares and saves in gallery or avatar code. android:tint is ignored for every PNG set with setImageResource. The previous drawable keeps its callback to this view.
items.suggested_fix: Route both through setImageDrawable(new BitmapDrawable(getResources(), bitmap)) (or getContext().getDrawable(resid)) so the drawable state stays consistent.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/ImageView.java: setImageBitmap(Bitmap bitmap) must call setImageDrawable(bitmap != null ? new android.graphics.drawable.BitmapDrawable(getResources(), bitmap) : null), as AOSP does. In setImageResource, replace the bitmap path's direct native_setDrawable call with setImageDrawable(bitmap != null ? new BitmapDrawable(getResources(), bitmap) : null), keeping the decodeResource call and the .xml branch. Keep assigning the bitmap field. getDrawable() then returns the current drawable, and the colorFilter is applied by setImageDrawable.
items.why_local: Small Java change. AOSP setImageBitmap wraps the bitmap in a BitmapDrawable and calls setImageDrawable. BitmapDrawable(Resources, Bitmap) here already builds the paintable from bitmap.getTexture(), so behaviour stays the same while the drawable and tint state become correct.

items.title: ImageView.setColorFilter(...) overloads are all empty
items.android_behavior: AOSP applies the color filter to the image drawable. This is the standard way to tint icons at runtime, for example imageView.setColorFilter(ContextCompat.getColor(..)) to switch an icon to the theme or accent colour or show a selected state.
items.impact: Icons tinted at runtime keep their original colour: often black-on-dark or white-on-white icons, and no selected or unselected feedback. Very many apps tint toolbar or list icons this way.
items.suggested_fix: Store the filter in colorFilter and reapply it to the current drawable (mutate + setColorFilter), the same way setImageTintList already does.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/ImageView.java: setColorFilter(ColorFilter cf): set this.colorFilter = cf, then call setImageDrawable(drawable) to reapply, exactly like setImageTintList does. setColorFilter(int color, PorterDuff.Mode mode): call setColorFilter(new PorterDuffColorFilter(color, mode)). setColorFilter(int color): call setColorFilter(color, PorterDuff.Mode.SRC_ATOP), the AOSP default. clearColorFilter(): set colorFilter = null and, if drawable != null, call drawable.setColorFilter(null), so the old filter is actually removed. No native changes.
items.why_local: One Java file. setImageTintList already shows the pattern (set the colorFilter field, then reapply via setImageDrawable), and the AOSP semantics are unambiguous.

items.title: Color.colorToHSV and HSVToColor give wrong results (hue offsets and a fraction multiplied by 6)
items.android_behavior: Hue is in [0,360): 60*((g-b)/d mod 6) when red is max, 60*((b-r)/d + 2) when green is max, 60*((r-g)/d + 4) when blue is max, and 0 for greys. HSVToColor uses f = h/60 - floor(h/60), in [0,1).
items.impact: Green-dominant colours get a hue 120 degrees too high and blue-dominant colours a hue past 360. Reds with g<b get a negative hue, and greys get 360. HSVToColor blows up the intermediate values (q and t go negative) for any hue not on a 60-degree boundary. Apps that darken or lighten theme colours with HSV (status bar from toolbar colour, colour pickers, palette-based theming, pressed-state shades) get the wrong colours. Example: colorToHSV(0xFF00FF00) gives hue 240 (blue) instead of 120.
items.suggested_fix: Use the standard formulas: green branch 2 + (b-r)/d, blue branch 4 + (r-g)/d, red branch ((g-b)/d) with a negative result +6, greys hue 0. In HSVToColor, f = h/60 - floor(h/60). Also normalise h with ((h % 360) + 360) % 360.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/Color.java, fix colorToHSV to use the standard RGB->HSV formula: if delta == 0 then hue = 0; else if max == red then hue = (green - blue) / delta; else if max == green then hue = 2 + (blue - red) / delta; else hue = 4 + (red - green) / delta. Then hue *= 60 and if (hue < 0) hue += 360. Store it in hsv[0]. Remove the '% 6', the extra '+ 2' and '+ 4', and the 'hsv[0] = 6'. Saturation (delta/max, 0 when max == 0) and value (max) stay as they are. In HSVToColor, clamp h to [0,360) first (if h < 0 or h >= 360 use 0, as AOSP does), clamp s and v to [0,1], and compute f as 'h / 60 - (float)Math.floor(h / 60)' WITHOUT the '* 6'. Leave the hi switch unchanged.
items.why_local: Pure Java maths with an unambiguous standard definition (AOSP's SkRGBToHSV/SkHSVToColor). Fossify's darkenColor/lightenColor and its colour pickers rely on it.

items.title: addOnAttachStateChangeListener keeps only one listener, so each call replaces the previous one
items.android_behavior: AOSP keeps a CopyOnWriteArrayList of listeners and notifies all of them. AndroidX relies on this: Fragment/ViewTreeLifecycleOwner, Compose's AndroidComposeView and DisposeOnDetachedFromWindow, RecyclerView, Glide's ViewTarget, coroutines' view scopes and Snackbar each register their own listener on the same view.
items.impact: When a second library registers a listener, the first one never fires. Compose content may not dispose or recompose correctly, image loads are not cleared, and lifecycle-scoped jobs leak or never start. These failures are silent and depend on registration order.
items.suggested_fix: Use a CopyOnWriteArrayList<OnAttachStateChangeListener> (as for on_layout_change_listeners) and iterate it in onAttachedToWindow/onDetachedFromWindow. Also dispatch from dispatchAttachedToWindow so that subclasses overriding onAttachedToWindow without calling super still notify listeners.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/View.java, replace the field `private OnAttachStateChangeListener onAttachStateChangeListener;` with `private final java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList<OnAttachStateChangeListener> attachStateListeners = new java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();` (AOSP uses CopyOnWriteArrayList because listeners often remove themselves inside the callback). addOnAttachStateChangeListener(l): attachStateListeners.add(l). removeOnAttachStateChangeListener(l): attachStateListeners.remove(l). In onAttachedToWindow(): `for (OnAttachStateChangeListener l : attachStateListeners) l.onViewAttachedToWindow(this);`. In onDetachedFromWindow(): the same with onViewDetachedFromWindow(this). Leave the keepScreenOn and floating_observer code as it is. Use the explicit class name or add the import, and remove every other use of the old field.
items.why_local: Confirmed: one field (View.java:1726, 2478-2483) holds only one listener, and onAttachedToWindow/onDetachedFromWindow call just that one. Turning it into a list is a small change in one file, AOSP behaviour is clear, and a reviewer can check it from the diff.

items.title: TextView.setCompoundDrawablesWithIntrinsicBounds / ...Relative... are empty, XML drawableStart/Left/Top are never read, and getCompoundDrawables returns an empty array
items.android_behavior: AOSP sets each drawable's bounds to its intrinsic size and calls setCompoundDrawables. It also reads android:drawableLeft/Start/Top/Right/End/Bottom in the constructor, and getCompoundDrawables returns the drawables currently set. These are the main ways apps put icons next to text in labels, menu rows and settings rows. A grep for TextView_drawable in api-impl finds no reader.
items.impact: Icons next to text never show, whether set from XML or from code with the WithIntrinsicBounds variants, which nearly every app uses. Code that reads getCompoundDrawables()[i] to tint or animate an icon gets null and either crashes or does nothing.
items.suggested_fix: Implement the WithIntrinsicBounds variants as AOSP does (setBounds(0,0,getIntrinsicWidth,getIntrinsicHeight), then setCompoundDrawables). Read the TextView_drawable* attributes in the constructor. Return the stored drawableLeft/Top/Right/Bottom from getCompoundDrawables and getCompoundDrawablesRelative.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/TextView.java: (1) setCompoundDrawablesWithIntrinsicBounds(Drawable l,t,r,b): for each non-null drawable call d.setBounds(0, 0, d.getIntrinsicWidth(), d.getIntrinsicHeight()), then call setCompoundDrawables(l, t, r, b), as AOSP does. (2) The int overload: Context c = getContext(); call the Drawable overload with (id != 0 ? c.getDrawable(id) : null) for each of the four ids. (3) setCompoundDrawablesRelativeWithIntrinsicBounds (both overloads): forward to the non-relative version with start->left and end->right (LTR only). (4) getCompoundDrawables() and getCompoundDrawablesRelative(): return new Drawable[] {drawableLeft, drawableTop, drawableRight, drawableBottom} (the existing private fields). (5) In the constructor's try block: read a.getDrawable for TextView_drawableLeft (fall back to TextView_drawableStart), TextView_drawableTop, TextView_drawableRight (fall back to TextView_drawableEnd) and TextView_drawableBottom. If any is non-null, call setCompoundDrawablesWithIntrinsicBounds(left, top, right, bottom). Do not touch Button/EditText overrides or native code.
items.why_local: Java-only and single-file. Native setCompoundDrawables already works, and the missing wrappers are simple AOSP code with clear semantics: set intrinsic bounds, then forward. Reading the XML drawables in the constructor adds about 10 lines that follow an existing pattern.

items.title: Context.getColor/getColorStateList resolve without the context theme
items.android_behavior: AOSP Context.getColor(id) is getResources().getColor(id, getTheme()) and getColorStateList(id) is getResources().getColorStateList(id, getTheme()). ContextCompat.getColor uses these on API 23+.
items.impact: Color resources defined as selectors that reference ?attr (common in Material/AppCompat apps, e.g. res/color/*.xml using ?attr/colorPrimary or colorOnSurface) are inflated without a theme. ColorStateList inflation then falls back to Color.MAGENTA, so text and icons come out magenta or with unresolved colors.
items.suggested_fix: Pass getTheme() in both methods (getColor(resId, getTheme()), getColorStateList(id, getTheme())).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/Context.java: change `public int getColor(int resId)` to `return this.getResources().getColor(resId, getTheme());` and change `public final ColorStateList getColorStateList(int id)` to `return getResources().getColorStateList(id, getTheme());`. This matches AOSP Context.getColor/getColorStateList, which resolve ?attr references in colour selectors against the context theme. Change nothing else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: Context.getColor and getColorStateList pass a null theme. AOSP passes getTheme(), and Resources.getColor(id, Theme) and getColorStateList(id, Theme) already exist. It is a two-line Java change.

items.title: ArgbEvaluator.getInstance() returns null, so ValueAnimator/ObjectAnimator.ofArgb and XML color animators get no evaluator
items.android_behavior: getInstance() returns a shared singleton ArgbEvaluator. ofArgb() and AnimatorInflater use it (for valueType=colorType, or when values are #colors) so colors blend per channel.
items.impact: ValueAnimator.ofArgb, ObjectAnimator.ofArgb (e.g. on setBackgroundColor or setTextColor) and color objectAnimators in res/animator XML interpolate the packed int, showing wrong intermediate colors. setEvaluator(null) is silently skipped. App code calling ArgbEvaluator.getInstance().evaluate(...) gets an NPE.
items.suggested_fix: private static final ArgbEvaluator sInstance = new ArgbEvaluator(); return sInstance. Also needs the PropertyValuesHolder fix so the evaluator is used for int values.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/animation/ArgbEvaluator.java add `private static final ArgbEvaluator sInstance = new ArgbEvaluator();` and make `getInstance()` return `sInstance` (AOSP does exactly this). Leave evaluate() as it is. For the color to actually be used on int values, idx 25 (PropertyValuesHolder using the evaluator for int values) must also be fixed.
items.why_local: A one-line fix with unambiguous AOSP behaviour: return a static singleton.

items.title: Path.addCircle is a logging stub (circular clips, avatars, ring cut-outs draw nothing)
items.evidence: A one-line delegation to the existing addOval(l,t,r,b,dir). The audit only mentions it inside M21 (Path.Direction), as a side note.
items.fix_hint: Replace the body of addCircle(float x, float y, float radius, Direction direction) with: addOval(x - radius, y - radius, x + radius, y + radius, direction);
items.why_local: A one-line delegation to the existing addOval(l,t,r,b,dir). The audit only mentions it inside M21 (Path.Direction), as a side note.

items.title: StateListDrawable inflates items without the theme, so ?attr references in selector items don't resolve
items.android_behavior: AOSP StateListDrawable.inflateChildElements uses obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawableItem), so items like android:drawable="?attr/selectableItemBackground" or "?attr/colorAccent" resolve against the current theme.
items.impact: Selectors whose items point at theme attributes (very common in AppCompat and Material themes and app styles) get null or unresolved drawables. That item then has no drawable or throws 'requires a drawable attribute', so themed pressed and checked states or whole backgrounds go missing.
items.suggested_fix: Use Drawable.obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, ...) (the helper already exists in Drawable) for both TypedArrays, as LayerDrawable and GradientDrawable already do.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/drawable/StateListDrawable.java, replace both 'r.obtainAttributes(attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawable)' (in inflate) and 'r.obtainAttributes(attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawableItem)' (in inflateChildElements) with the static helper inherited from Drawable: 'obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawable)' and 'obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawableItem)'. The helper uses theme.obtainStyledAttributes when theme != null, so ?attr references resolve. Change nothing else.
items.why_local: A two-line change that replaces r.obtainAttributes with the existing theme-aware Drawable.obtainAttributes helper, exactly as AOSP StateListDrawable does.

items.title: Theme.applyStyle/setTo never update ThemeKey, so every Theme shares one drawable/ColorStateList cache bucket
items.android_behavior: AOSP Theme.applyStyle calls mKey.append(resId, force) and setTo copies mKey. ThemedResourceCache (used by loadDrawable via mDrawableCacheInternal.put(key, theme, cs) and by the ComplexColor cache) partitions cached entries by that key, so a drawable or ColorStateList resolved against one theme is not reused for another.
items.impact: All non-null themes have an empty, equal ThemeKey. A drawable or color selector whose ?attr values were resolved under one theme (e.g. the activity theme) is handed to views under a different theme (ThemeOverlay toolbar, dialog theme, a second activity with another theme). This gives wrong icon tints, ripple and selector colors and dark/light mismatches in Material/AppCompat apps that use overlays.
items.suggested_fix: In Theme.applyStyle add mKey.append(resid, force). In Theme.setTo add mKey.setTo(other.getKey()) (and recompute the hash code in ThemeKey.setTo as AOSP does). Implement rebase() from the key if needed.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/res/Resources.java: (1) In Theme.applyStyle(int resid, boolean force), after `mAssets.applyThemeStyle(theme, resid, force);` add `mKey.append(resid, force);` (AOSP ResourcesImpl.ThemeImpl.applyStyle does this). (2) In Theme.setTo(Theme other), after `getAssets().copyTheme(this.theme, other.theme);` add `mKey.setTo(other.mKey);`. (3) In static class ThemeKey, method setTo(ThemeKey other), add `mHashCode = other.mHashCode;` after `mCount = other.mCount;` (AOSP copies the hash too; without it equals() fails on the hashCode comparison). Do not change anything else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: Theme.mKey is never appended, so every Theme hashes to the same ThemedResourceCache bucket. ThemeKey.setTo also fails to copy mHashCode. The AOSP fix is three small lines in one file, and a reviewer can check them against AOSP. It does change which cached drawables and colours each theme gets, so the reviewer should look at it carefully.

items.title: ProgressBar/SeekBar ignore android:max and android:progress from XML
items.android_behavior: android:max and android:progress set the range and initial value. Seekbars for volume (max=15), seconds (max=60) and so on rely on this.
items.impact: A SeekBar declared with max="10" still ranges 0..100, so the values reported to the app are 10x too large. A ProgressBar with max=1000 clamps setProgress(500) to 100 (full bar). Initial progress from XML is not shown.
items.suggested_fix: Read ProgressBar_max, ProgressBar_min and ProgressBar_progress in the constructor and call setMax and setProgress (SeekBar's overrides then update the GtkRange).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/ProgressBar.java, constructor ProgressBar(Context, AttributeSet, int), before a.recycle(): call setMax(a.getInt(com.android.internal.R.styleable.ProgressBar_max, max)); then setProgress(a.getInt(com.android.internal.R.styleable.ProgressBar_progress, progress)). This order matches AOSP: max first, then progress. Use the virtual setters (not field assignments) so SeekBar's overrides update the GtkRange. Do not change the SeekBar C code.
items.why_local: A few lines in the ProgressBar constructor, using the existing virtual setMax/setProgress (SeekBar's overrides already call native_setMax and native_setProgress). The AOSP attribute semantics are clear.

items.title: TextPaint(Paint), TextPaint(int flags) and TextPaint.set() drop the source paint even though Paint(Paint)/set(Paint) exist
items.android_behavior: new TextPaint(paint) copies color, text size, typeface, flags and so on from the source. set(tp) copies all Paint fields as well. Paint(Paint) and Paint.set(Paint) are implemented in ATL (native_clone).
items.impact: Custom views and libraries that copy a paint (new TextPaint(getPaint()), new TextPaint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG), tp.set(textView.getPaint())) draw text in the default black, small, regular font instead of the configured style. This affects chips and badges, chart labels, ellipsizing helpers and Compose/AndroidX text measuring.
items.suggested_fix: Call super(p) and super(flags), and uncomment super.set(tp). Also copy the TextPaint-specific fields in the Paint constructor when p is a TextPaint.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/text/TextPaint.java: change `TextPaint(int flags)` to call `super(flags);`, change `TextPaint(Paint p)` to call `super(p);`, and in `set(TextPaint tp)` restore the first line `super.set(tp);` (Paint.set(Paint) exists and clones the native paint). Keep the field copies that follow. This is exactly AOSP TextPaint.
items.why_local: Paint(Paint), Paint(int) and Paint.set(Paint) already exist in graphics/Paint.java, so the fix just uncomments three super calls in TextPaint.java, which matches AOSP exactly.

items.title: NetworkCapabilities never includes NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED, and NetworkInfo.isAvailable() is always false, so connected networks look unusable
items.android_behavior: A working default network has INTERNET and VALIDATED (plus NOT_SUSPENDED, NOT_ROAMING, NOT_CONGESTED, NOT_VCN_MANAGED). NetworkInfo.isAvailable() is true for a connected network and getTypeName() returns "WIFI" for TYPE_WIFI.
items.impact: Many 'isOnline()' helpers check hasCapability(INTERNET) && hasCapability(VALIDATED), or info.isAvailable() && info.isConnected(), and show 'No internet connection' while online. WorkManager's NetworkConnectedController (API 26+) requires isValidated, so jobs with a CONNECTED network constraint (sync, backups, feed refresh) never run. Old 'Wi-Fi only' checks comparing getTypeName() to "WIFI" fail.
items.suggested_fix: When nativeGetNetworkAvailable() is true (or GNetworkMonitor connectivity == FULL), also add NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED, NOT_SUSPENDED, NOT_ROAMING and NOT_CONGESTED. NetworkInfo.isAvailable() should return state == CONNECTED, and getTypeName() should return "WIFI" when connected.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/net/ConnectivityManager.java getNetworkCapabilities(): after adding NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET, also call `capabilities.addCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED);` (this code only runs when nativeGetNetworkAvailable() is true). In src/api-impl/android/net/NetworkInfo.java: make `isAvailable()` return `state == State.CONNECTED`, and make `getTypeName()` return `state == State.CONNECTED ? "WIFI" : "UNKNOWN"` to match getType() returning TYPE_WIFI (1). Check that NetworkCapabilities.addCapability supports value 16 (NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED is already defined).
items.why_local: A small Java-only change in two files with clear AOSP semantics: a connected internet network is VALIDATED, isAvailable() is true when connected, and the type name is "WIFI" because getType() already reports TYPE_WIFI.

items.title: Settings.Secure/Global.getString return sentinel strings ("NOTICEME", "STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_...") instead of null; android_id is not hex
items.android_behavior: Unknown or unset settings return null. ANDROID_ID is a 64-bit value as 16 lowercase hex digits. getInt/getFloat without a default throw SettingNotFoundException rather than returning -1/0.
items.impact: Apps that check getString(...) != null and then use the value show or parse junk. For example, Settings.Global 'device_name' displays 'STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_device_name', and default_input_method / enabled_accessibility_services get parsed as component names. Apps converting ANDROID_ID with Long.parseLong(id,16) or new BigInteger(id,16) crash with NumberFormatException, and every install shares one ID. try/catch(SettingNotFoundException) fallbacks never trigger and get -1/0.0 instead.
items.suggested_fix: Return null for unknown keys and log once. Generate a per-install random 16-hex-digit android_id stored in the app's data dir. Throw SettingNotFoundException from the no-default getInt/getFloat variants.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/provider/Settings.java: in Secure.getString, keep the Slog.w warning for unknown keys but return null instead of "NOTICEME". Make "android_id" return a fixed 16-character lowercase hex string (AOSP returns a 64-bit value in hex), e.g. `String.format("%016x", <some fixed long constant>)`; it must be stable across calls. In Global.getString, also return null in the default case instead of "STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_" + key. Leave advertising_id and the int/float getters unchanged. If System.getString has the same sentinel pattern, apply the same null default there.
items.why_local: A small Java-only change in one file. AOSP semantics are clear: unknown settings return null, and android_id is a 16-character lowercase hex string.

items.title: selectDrawable(-1) keeps showing the previous child instead of clearing it
items.android_behavior: AOSP DrawableContainer.selectDrawable(idx) with idx < 0 sets mCurrDrawable = null and mCurIndex = -1, so a selector whose items don't match the current state draws nothing.
items.impact: Selectors without a default item (e.g. only state_pressed or state_checked items, common for foregrounds, list selectors, highlight overlays and check marks) stick on their last matched drawable. A pressed or checked highlight stays visible after release or uncheck.
items.suggested_fix: When idx < 0 (or the slot is null), set curIndex = -1, call native_selectChild(paintable, 0) (and let the native side handle a NULL child), invalidateSelf(), and return true if curIndex changed.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/drawable/DrawableContainer.java, change selectDrawable(int idx) so that an idx that is negative or >= state.childCount clears the selection, as AOSP does: if (idx < 0 || idx >= state.childCount) { if (curIndex == -1) return false; curIndex = -1; native_selectChild(paintable, 0); invalidateSelf(); return true; }. Keep the existing branch for valid indices unchanged (still return false when idx == curIndex). Do not touch the C code: the native side already treats a 0 child pointer as 'no child'.
items.why_local: Small, unambiguous AOSP behaviour. The native container paintable already handles a NULL child (snapshot and intrinsic size check child != NULL), so passing 0 is safe.

items.title: DrawableContainer.setBounds skips super and never gives newly selected children bounds
items.android_behavior: The container keeps its own bounds (getBounds() returns them, and onBoundsChange forwards them) and copies them to whichever child becomes current in selectDrawable.
items.impact: getBounds()/copyBounds() on any StateListDrawable, LevelListDrawable or AnimationDrawable return 0x0, which breaks compound-drawable layout and custom views that size from getBounds(). When the drawable is drawn through Java (inside a LayerDrawable, ripple, inset or custom view), a child selected after a state change keeps empty or stale bounds and draws nothing, or draws in the wrong place.
items.suggested_fix: Call super.setBounds(...) (or override onBoundsChange) and, in selectDrawable, call newChild.setBounds(getBounds()), setState(getState()), setLevel(getLevel()) and copy alpha/colour filter, as AOSP does.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/drawable/DrawableContainer.java: (1) remove the setBounds(int,int,int,int) override and add instead '@Override protected void onBoundsChange(Rect bounds) { if (curIndex != -1 && state.drawables[curIndex] != null) state.drawables[curIndex].setBounds(bounds); }' (import android.graphics.Rect). Drawable.setBounds stores mBounds and calls onBoundsChange when they change. (2) In selectDrawable, after 'curIndex = idx;', call 'state.drawables[idx].setBounds(getBounds());' so the newly selected child gets the container's current bounds (AOSP DrawableContainer.selectDrawable does d.setBounds(getBounds()) on the new child). Do not change draw().
items.why_local: Small Java-only change with clear AOSP semantics: the container keeps its own bounds and gives them to the current child and to each newly selected child.

items.title: withEndAction/withStartAction are never cleared and re-run on every later animate() call
items.android_behavior: AOSP attaches start/end actions to the single animation being started; they run once and are not inherited by the next animate() call. The end action also does not run when the animation is cancelled.
items.impact: The common 'animate().alpha(0).withEndAction(() -> v.setVisibility(GONE))' followed later by 'animate().alpha(1)' runs the old GONE action again, and the view disappears after fading in. Cancelling also triggers the end action. Visible in show/hide toggles, toasts and snackbars.
items.suggested_fix: Capture startAction/endAction in local variables in start(), set the fields to null, attach them only to that animator, and skip endAction when the animation was cancelled.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/ViewPropertyAnimator.java start(): before adding the listener, copy the actions into locals (`final Runnable start = startAction; final Runnable end = endAction;`), then set the fields to null (`startAction = null; endAction = null;`). In the anonymous AnimatorListener, use the locals instead of the fields (`if (start != null) start.run();` and `if (end != null) end.run();`), and change the condition to `if (start != null || end != null)`. AOSP runs withStartAction/withEndAction for the next animation only. Leave setListener's persistent behaviour unchanged.
items.why_local: Confirmed: the endAction and startAction fields are never cleared, and the anonymous listener reads them when it fires, so a later animate() runs old actions again. AOSP ties these actions to a single animation, and the fix is a few lines in start().

items.title: Button.setText(null) shows "null"; Button and EditText don't override setText(CharSequence, BufferType), so that path writes into the wrong native widget
items.android_behavior: setText(null) clears the text. setText(text, BufferType.EDITABLE/SPANNABLE) sets the text on any TextView subclass.
items.impact: Buttons fed a null string literally read "null". editText.setText(str, TextView.BufferType.EDITABLE), a common idiom, runs TextView's native_setText, whose box_get_label walks the children of a GtkText or GtkButton instead of the label box. The text is not set, and GTK prints criticals or crashes.
items.suggested_fix: Use text == null ? "" : text.toString() in Button, and override setText(CharSequence, BufferType) in Button, EditText and CompoundButton to route to their own native setters.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/Button.java: change setText(CharSequence text) to native_setText(widget, text == null ? "" : text.toString()) (AOSP treats null as empty), and add @Override public void setText(CharSequence text, BufferType type) { setText(text); }. In src/api-impl/android/widget/EditText.java: add the same override, @Override public void setText(CharSequence text, BufferType type) { setText(text); }. Both classes already override setText(CharSequence), so there is no recursion. Import android.widget.TextView.BufferType if needed (it is the nested TextView.BufferType). Do not touch the native code.
items.why_local: Java-only overrides in two files with obvious semantics. Without them, TextView.setText(CharSequence, BufferType) calls the TextView native on a GtkButton/GtkText widget.

items.title: PropertyValuesHolder ignores the evaluator for int/float values and ignores keyframes, so ofArgb/ArgbEvaluator color animations interpolate raw ints
items.android_behavior: AOSP stores values in a KeyframeSet and always runs them through the TypeEvaluator when one is set (ValueAnimator.ofInt(...).setEvaluator(new ArgbEvaluator()) is the standard color-animation idiom). Keyframes from ofKeyframe() are animated. Fractions outside [0,1] from Overshoot/Anticipate interpolators extrapolate past the end values. clone() copies the evaluator.
items.impact: Any color animation that uses setEvaluator(new ArgbEvaluator()) on int values (toolbar or status-bar color fades, button highlight, Material components) interpolates the packed ARGB int linearly and flashes through unrelated colors. ofKeyframe() animators log 'No values set' and leave the value as a Keyframe object. Overshoot and bounce interpolators are clamped and lose the overshoot. clone() drops the evaluator, so cloned color animators break even with an evaluator.
items.suggested_fix: In calculateValue, when evaluator != null, use it for the int, float and object paths (boxing values). Implement keyframe evaluation: find the surrounding keyframes and apply per-keyframe interpolators. Remove the [0,1] clamp and extrapolate using the first and last segments as AOSP does. Copy the evaluator in clone().
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/animation/PropertyValuesHolder.java, method calculateValue(float fraction): in the values_int branch, when `evaluator != null`, set `value = evaluator.evaluate(f, values_int[i], values_int[i >= values_int.length - 1 ? i : i + 1]);` (autoboxed Integers) instead of the linear int formula; keep the existing linear formula only for evaluator == null. Do the same in the values_float branch (evaluator.evaluate(f, values_float[i], values_float[next]) when evaluator != null). Use the same index clamping as the existing values_object branch so a length-1 array or fraction==1 never reads past the end. AOSP: PropertyValuesHolder uses mEvaluator whenever it is set (needed for ArgbEvaluator on int color values). Do NOT touch keyframes in this task. Pair it with idx 95 (ArgbEvaluator.getInstance).
items.why_local: The evaluator half is a small, unambiguous change inside calculateValue() in one file: AOSP always calls the PVH's evaluator when one is set. Keyframe support is a separate, larger job (it ties in with idx 97), so it is left out of this task.

items.title: <include> ignores android:visibility (and other overrides besides id and layout_*) on the include tag
items.android_behavior: AOSP's parseInclude reads View_id and View_visibility from the include tag and applies both to the included root (VISIBLE/INVISIBLE/GONE).
items.impact: The very common '<include layout="@layout/empty_state" android:visibility="gone"/>' (also used for loading/error overlays) is shown at startup, overlapping real content until code hides it.
items.suggested_fix: Also read com.android.internal.R.attr.visibility from the include attrs and call view.setVisibility(VISIBILITY_FLAGS[value]) when it is present.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/LayoutInflater.java parseInclude(), where it reads the id with `context.obtainStyledAttributes(attrs, new int[] {com.android.internal.R.attr.id})`, read visibility too: use `new int[] {com.android.internal.R.attr.id, com.android.internal.R.attr.visibility}` (the ids stay in ascending order), and after setting the id add `int visibility = ta.getInt(1, -1);` before ta.recycle(). Then, as AOSP does: `switch (visibility) { case 0: view.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE); break; case 1: view.setVisibility(View.INVISIBLE); break; case 2: view.setVisibility(View.GONE); break; }` (the XML enum is visible=0, invisible=1, gone=2; -1 means not set, so leave the view as it is). Do this before group.addView(view). Only the non-merge branch changes.
items.why_local: Confirmed: parseInclude only reads android:id from the include tag. AOSP also reads android:visibility and applies it, a few lines in one method. com.android.internal.R.attr.visibility exists (0x010100dc).

items.title: Intent copy constructor and putExtras alias Bundles instead of copying/merging; copies drop flags/type/package
items.android_behavior: AOSP copies extras (new Bundle(o.mExtras)) and copies flags, type, package, categories, selector and clipData. putExtras merges with mExtras.putAll(), keeping existing extras. getExtras() returns a copy, or null when there are no extras.
items.impact: putExtra(...) followed by putExtras(bundle) loses the earlier extras. Later putExtra calls write into the caller's Bundle, and modifying a copied Intent mutates the original. new Intent(other) loses FLAG_ACTIVITY_* flags and the MIME type. Wrong data is passed between activities, services and PendingIntents.
items.suggested_fix: Copy constructor: this.extras = o.extras != null ? new Bundle(o.extras) : null, and copy flags, type, packageName, selector and categories. putExtras: extras.putAll(src). getExtras: return a copy.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/Intent.java only. (1) Constructor Intent(Intent o): copy action, data, component, plus `this.flags = o.flags; this.type = o.type; this.packageName = o.packageName; this.selector = o.selector;` and set `this.extras = o.extras != null ? new Bundle(o.extras) : new Bundle();` instead of sharing the Bundle (AOSP copies the extras Bundle). (2) putExtras(Bundle extras): replace the body with `if (extras != null) this.extras.putAll(extras); return this;` (AOSP merges into the existing extras). (3) putExtras(Intent src): replace the body with `if (src.extras != null) this.extras.putAll(src.extras); return this;`. Remove the two `// FIXME HACK` comments. Never set this.extras to null, because native code (util.c intent_serialize) dereferences it. Do not touch replaceExtras.
items.why_local: Confirmed: the copy constructor aliases the extras Bundle and drops flags, type, package and selector, and both putExtras overloads replace the extras instead of merging them. This is pure Java with clear AOSP semantics. extras must stay non-null because native intent_serialize reads it.

items.title: scrollTo/setScrollX/setScrollY never call onScrollChanged or the scroll-change listener (setOnScrollChangeListener is empty)
items.android_behavior: In AOSP, scrollTo only acts when the position changes; it then calls onScrollChanged(x, y, oldX, oldY), notifies the OnScrollChangeListener and invalidates. setScrollX/Y go through scrollTo.
items.impact: Custom views and libraries that override onScrollChanged (parallax headers, ScrollView subclasses, sticky headers, scroll-to-hide toolbars), and apps using View.setOnScrollChangeListener, get no callbacks. setScrollX/Y also do not redraw.
items.suggested_fix: In scrollTo: if (x != scrollX || y != scrollY) { int ox = scrollX, oy = scrollY; scrollX = x; scrollY = y; onScrollChanged(x, y, ox, oy); if (on_scroll_change_listener != null) on_scroll_change_listener.onScrollChange(this, x, y, ox, oy); invalidate(); }. Store the listener in the setter and route setScrollX/Y through scrollTo.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/View.java: (1) setOnScrollChangeListener(l) stores it: `on_scroll_change_listener = l;`. (2) onScrollChanged(int l, int t, int oldl, int oldt) calls the listener: `if (on_scroll_change_listener != null) on_scroll_change_listener.onScrollChange(this, l, t, oldl, oldt);` (this matches AOSP View.onScrollChanged). (3) scrollTo(x, y): `if (scrollX != x || scrollY != y) { int oldX = scrollX; int oldY = scrollY; scrollX = x; scrollY = y; onScrollChanged(scrollX, scrollY, oldX, oldY); invalidate(); }`. Do nothing when the position is unchanged, as AOSP does. (4) setScrollX(value) becomes scrollTo(value, scrollY), and setScrollY(value) becomes scrollTo(scrollX, value). Do not change getScrollX/getScrollY.
items.why_local: Confirmed: scrollTo never calls onScrollChanged, setOnScrollChangeListener does not store the listener, and setScrollX/Y bypass scrollTo. AOSP does this in a few lines, all in View.java.

items.title: Window.addFlags/setFlags/clearFlags are empty: FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON, FLAG_FULLSCREEN and others are ignored and not reflected in getAttributes()
items.android_behavior: AOSP updates mWindowAttributes.flags and applies them. FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON (0x80) keeps the display awake and FLAG_FULLSCREEN (0x400) hides the status bar. The constant is 128, not 0. The 5-argument LayoutParams constructor stores type, flags and format.
items.impact: Video players, games, navigation, recipe and timer apps call getWindow().addFlags(FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON). The screen still blanks, even though ATL already has native_keep_screen_on for View.setKeepScreenOn. Games that use FLAG_FULLSCREEN do not go fullscreen. getAttributes().flags reads back 0, and popup windows lose their type and flags.
items.suggested_fix: Keep params.flags = (params.flags & ~mask) | (flags & mask). Map the 0x80 bit to native_keep_screen_on on the decor view and 0x400 to nativeSetFullscreen. Fix FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON to 0x80 and store type/flags/format in the LayoutParams constructor.
items.fix_hint: (1) In src/api-impl/android/view/WindowManager.java LayoutParams: set FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON = 0x00000080 (the AOSP value). Make the constructor LayoutParams(int w, int h, int type, int flags, int format) store `this.type = type; this.flags = flags; this.format = format;` after super(w, h). (2) In src/api-impl/android/view/Window.java: addFlags(flags) calls setFlags(flags, flags); clearFlags(flags) calls setFlags(0, flags); setFlags(flags, mask) does `params.flags = (params.flags & ~mask) | (flags & mask);` and then `decorView.setKeepScreenOn((params.flags & WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON) != 0);`. AOSP Window.setFlags updates getAttributes().flags the same way. Do not try to implement any other flag.
items.why_local: Bookkeeping the flags in params.flags, fixing the FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON constant and storing the constructor arguments are mechanical. Keep-screen-on can then use the existing View.setKeepScreenOn on the decor view, so no native work is needed. FLAG_FULLSCREEN stays out of scope.

items.title: AudioManager reports ringer mode SILENT and stream volume 0
items.evidence: One file. The values are AOSP constants, and the honest model (an in-memory volume table) is easy to check. Today getRingerMode()==0 is RINGER_MODE_SILENT, so apps that respect silent mode (alarms, notification sounds, keypad tones) stay quiet, and 0 volume reads as muted.

Keep a static int[] volumes (index by streamType, guard bounds) initialised to getStreamMaxVolume(); getStreamVolume returns it, setStreamVolume clamps to [0,max] and stores it, add adjustStreamVolume(stream, direction, flags) changing it by 1 step. Add getStreamMinVolume(int) returning 0.
items.why_local: One file. The values are AOSP constants, and the honest model (an in-memory volume table) is easy to check. Today getRingerMode()==0 is RINGER_MODE_SILENT, so apps that respect silent mode (alarms, notification sounds, keypad tones) stay quiet, and 0 volume reads as muted.

items.title: AccountManager.addOnAccountsUpdatedListener(listener, handler, boolean) and android.content.SyncStatusObserver missing (Tasks.org crashes)
items.evidence: Missing API surface found in run mg-microg (org.tasks CRASH: NoSuchMethodError and ClassNotFoundException). AOSP semantics are simple, and ATL has no sync service, so a status-change listener that never fires is correct.
items.fix_hint: AccountManager: add the 3-arg overload addOnAccountsUpdatedListener(l, handler, updateImmediately) that calls the 4-arg one with null types. In the 4-arg one, when updateImmediately, post l.onAccountsUpdated(getAccounts()) to (handler != null ? handler : new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())). Keep listeners in a list, and have removeOnAccountsUpdatedListener remove them. New file SyncStatusObserver (SPDX header not needed for AOSP-style API files; follow neighbours): public interface SyncStatusObserver { void onStatusChanged(int which); }. ContentResolver: add SYNC_OBSERVER_TYPE_SETTINGS=1, PENDING=2, ACTIVE=4 constants; public static Object addStatusChangeListener(int mask, SyncStatusObserver callback) returns callback as the handle; public static void removeStatusChangeListener(Object handle) does nothing.
items.why_local: Missing API surface found in run mg-microg (org.tasks CRASH: NoSuchMethodError and ClassNotFoundException). AOSP semantics are simple, and ATL has no sync service, so a status-change listener that never fires is correct.

items.title: Framework PopupMenu Menu methods throw UnsupportedOperationException (add(CharSequence), add(int,int,int,int), removeItem, clear, setGroupVisible, hasVisibleItems, addSubMenu overloads)
items.evidence: One file. Each method reuses the existing add() and setVisible() bookkeeping. The only trap is native position bookkeeping, which is avoided by always hiding an item through setVisible(false) before removing it from the list.
items.fix_hint: Store groupId and order in MenuItemImpl from add(groupId,itemId,order,title). add(CharSequence t) calls add(0,0,0,t); add(int titleRes) calls add(0,0,0,mContext.getString(titleRes)); add(g,i,o,int titleRes) uses getString. addSubMenu(CharSequence) and addSubMenu(int) delegate to addSubMenu(0,0,0,title). removeItem(id): find the item in items, call item.setVisible(false), then items.remove(item). removeGroup(g): the same for every item with groupId==g (iterate over a copy). clear(): setVisible(false) on every item, then items.clear(). setGroupVisible(g,v): setVisible(v) on matching items. setGroupCheckable(g,c,excl): setCheckable(c) on matching items. hasVisibleItems(): numVisibleItems > 0. close(): calls PopupMenu.this.dismiss().
items.why_local: One file. Each method reuses the existing add() and setVisible() bookkeeping. The only trap is native position bookkeeping, which is avoided by always hiding an item through setVisible(false) before removing it from the list.

items.title: Vibrator has no vibrate(VibrationEffect); VibrationEffect drops its data; repeat index never loops
items.evidence: Two Java files and no native change: the native vibrate(long) already exists. AOSP semantics are clear (one-shot vs waveform with a repeat index). Apps on minSdk>=26, such as Fossify Clock alarms and timers, take the VibrationEffect path and hit NoSuchMethodError on the phone.
items.fix_hint: VibrationEffect: store long[] timings, int repeat (-1 = none) and long duration. createOneShot(ms, amp) gives duration=ms. createWaveform(long[] timings, int repeat) and add createWaveform(long[] timings, int[] amplitudes, int repeat) storing timings and repeat. Add DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE=-1 and createPredefined(int) (EFFECT_CLICK=0 -> 20 ms, EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK=1 -> 30 ms, EFFECT_TICK=2 -> 10 ms, EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK=5 -> 40 ms). Vibrator: add vibrate(VibrationEffect e) and vibrate(VibrationEffect e, AudioAttributes a), which call vibrate(e.duration) for one-shots and vibrate(e.timings, e.repeat) for waveforms; add hasAmplitudeControl() returning false. In vibrate(long[] pattern, int repeat), when repeat >= 0, after the first pass keep looping from index repeat until interrupted (cancel()); call cancel() before starting a new pattern.
items.why_local: Two Java files and no native change: the native vibrate(long) already exists. AOSP semantics are clear (one-shot vs waveform with a repeat index). Apps on minSdk>=26, such as Fossify Clock alarms and timers, take the VibrationEffect path and hit NoSuchMethodError on the phone.

items.title: ContentResolver.registerContentObserver/notifyChange are no-ops, so cursors and observers never refresh
items.evidence: An in-process observer registry in Java only. ContentObserver.dispatchChange already exists, and with the new MediaStore index (insert/update/delete) apps can now change data that other screens observe. AOSP's URI-tree matching is the subtle part, so the hint spells it out.
items.fix_hint: Keep a static synchronized List of entries {Uri uri, boolean descendants, ContentObserver observer}. register* adds (ignore userHandle), and unregisterContentObserver removes every entry with that observer. notifyChange(uri, observer[, sync]) calls entry.observer.dispatchChange(entry.observer == observer, uri) for each entry where: entry.uri equals uri; OR entry.descendants and uri is under entry.uri (same scheme and authority, and uri's path segments start with entry.uri's); OR entry.uri is under uri (observers registered below the changed uri are always notified). Skip an entry when entry.observer == observer && !observer.deliverSelfNotifications(). Copy the list before iterating. Also add notifyChange(Uri, ContentObserver, int flags). In ATLMediaStore insert/update/delete, after a successful change call getContext().getContentResolver().notifyChange(uri, null).
items.why_local: An in-process observer registry in Java only. ContentObserver.dispatchChange already exists, and with the new MediaStore index (insert/update/delete) apps can now change data that other screens observe. AOSP's URI-tree matching is the subtle part, so the hint spells it out.

items.title: Framework PopupMenu MenuItem methods throw UnsupportedOperationException (getTitle, isChecked, isEnabled, getGroupId, setShowAsAction, setTitle(int), item click listeners)
items.evidence: One file. These are store-and-return fields with the obvious MenuItem javadoc semantics. MenuInflater and apps call several of them on android.widget.PopupMenu menus, and today any of those calls crashes.
items.fix_hint: In MenuItemImpl add fields groupId, order, checkable, checked, enabled=true, titleCondensed, intent, OnMenuItemClickListener itemListener, Drawable icon. Implement: getTitle() returns title; setTitle(int) calls setTitle(mContext.getString(resId)); setTitle(CharSequence), when isVisible(), re-inserts the item (setVisible(false); setVisible(true)) so the GMenu label updates; setChecked/isChecked, setEnabled/isEnabled and setCheckable/isCheckable store and return the fields; getGroupId/getOrder return them; setShowAsAction(int) does nothing and setShowAsActionFlags returns this (popups have no action bar); setOnMenuItemClickListener stores it; setIntent stores it; setIcon(Drawable) stores it and setIcon(int) loads it via mContext.getDrawable; getIcon returns the field; hasSubMenu() returns subMenu != null; getTitleCondensed returns titleCondensed != null ? titleCondensed : title; setAlphabeticShortcut/setNumericShortcut/setIconTintList return this; getActionView returns null; isActionViewExpanded/expandActionView return false. In menuItemClickCallback: find the item; if its itemListener returns true stop; else if item.intent != null call mContext.startActivity(intent); else call mMenuItemClickListener. SubMenuImpl.setIcon returns this; clearHeader does nothing.
items.why_local: One file. These are store-and-return fields with the obvious MenuItem javadoc semantics. MenuInflater and apps call several of them on android.widget.PopupMenu menus, and today any of those calls crashes.

items.title: ProgressBar.setIndeterminate assigns the parameter instead of the field, so isIndeterminate() never changes
items.android_behavior: Updates mIndeterminate so isIndeterminate() reflects the call.
items.impact: Apps and libraries that check isIndeterminate() before switching to determinate progress (download and loading UIs) make the wrong decision.
items.suggested_fix: this.indeterminate = indeterminate;
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/ProgressBar.java, setIndeterminate(boolean indeterminate): replace `indeterminate = true;` with `this.indeterminate = indeterminate;` so isIndeterminate() reflects the last call, as in AOSP.
items.why_local: A clear one-line bug: the parameter shadows the field.

items.title: Editor.putX(key, null) stores null instead of removing the key
items.android_behavior: AOSP commitToMemory uses `if (v == this || v == null)`, so putString(key, null) / putStringSet(key, null) removes the key.
items.impact: contains(key) stays true after an app 'clears' a value with putString(key, null), and a null entry is written to the XML. Apps using contains() to detect first run or a logged-in state take the wrong branch.
items.suggested_fix: Change the condition to `if (v == this || v == null)`.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/app/SharedPreferencesImpl.java, in EditorImpl.commitToMemory, change the condition `if (v == this) { // magic value for a removal mutation` to `if (v == this || v == null) {` so that putString(key, null) and putStringSet(key, null) remove the key, as AOSP does ("v == this || v == null"). Change nothing else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: commitToMemory treats only the magic `this` value as a removal. AOSP treats `v == this || v == null` as a removal. It is a one-condition change.

items.title: CountDownTimer delays the first onTick by one interval
items.evidence:
stopTimeInFuture = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + millisInFuture;
handler.postDelayed(tickRunnable, countDownInterval);
items.android_behavior: AOSP start() sends the first message immediately, so onTick(≈millisInFuture) fires right away and then every interval.
items.impact: Countdown UIs (timers, OTP resend, workout apps) show nothing or a stale value for the first interval and get one tick fewer than on Android.
items.suggested_fix: Use handler.post(tickRunnable) for the first tick (and account for onTick execution time like AOSP).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/os/CountDownTimer.java, method start(): replace `handler.postDelayed(tickRunnable, countDownInterval);` with `handler.post(tickRunnable);` so the first onTick fires immediately, as in AOSP (mHandler.sendMessage(mHandler.obtainMessage(MSG))). Do not change tickRunnable.
items.why_local: Confirmed: start() uses postDelayed(tickRunnable, countDownInterval), but AOSP CountDownTimer.start() sends the first tick message immediately. The fix is one line.

items.title: Window.peekDecorView() returns null although the decor view always exists
items.android_behavior: AOSP returns the decor view once it has been created, which in ATL is always (it is built in the constructor).
items.impact: Code that uses peekDecorView() to find the window token or root (hide-keyboard helpers, AndroidX activity/ime helpers, dialog sizing code) takes the 'no window yet' branch and silently skips its work. The keyboard may not hide and window insets controllers are not set up.
items.suggested_fix: return decorView;
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/Window.java, change peekDecorView() to `return decorView;` (AOSP returns the decor view when it exists; here the constructor always creates it).
items.why_local: The decor view is created in the constructor and always exists, and AOSP peekDecorView returns mDecor, so returning the field is correct.

items.title: Activity.moveTaskToBack and setFinishOnTouchOutside are package-private
items.android_behavior: Both are public in AOSP. moveTaskToBack(true) is commonly called from onBackPressed to background the app instead of finishing it.
items.impact: Calls from app code (another package) fail with IllegalAccessError at runtime, crashing apps that override back to call moveTaskToBack(true) and dialog-themed activities that call setFinishOnTouchOutside.
items.suggested_fix: Make both public. Keep the no-op/true semantics, or minimize the window for moveTaskToBack.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/app/Activity.java, change `boolean moveTaskToBack(boolean nonroot)` to `public boolean moveTaskToBack(boolean nonroot)` and `void setFinishOnTouchOutside(boolean finish)` to `public void setFinishOnTouchOutside(boolean finish)`. Keep the bodies unchanged.
items.why_local: Confirmed: both methods are package-private, but they are public API in AOSP, so app bytecode that calls them fails with an IllegalAccessError. Changing the access modifiers is trivial.

items.title: Canvas.drawText(char[], index, count, ...) treats count as an end index
items.android_behavior: The AOSP signature is drawText(char[] text, int index, int count, float x, float y, Paint paint). It draws count characters starting at index.
items.impact: Any caller using the char[] overload with index > 0 draws the wrong substring, or throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when count < index (e.g. drawText(buf, 5, 3, ...)). GskCanvas does not override this, so view drawing hits it too: custom text views, chart labels, and libraries that keep char buffers.
items.suggested_fix: public void drawText(char[] text, int index, int count, float x, float y, Paint paint) { drawText(new String(text, index, count), x, y, paint); }
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/Canvas.java, change 'public void drawText(char text[], int start, int end, float x, float y, Paint paint)' so its parameters are (char[] text, int index, int count, ...) as in AOSP, and its body is 'drawText(new String(text, index, count), x, y, paint);'. The third argument is a character COUNT starting at index, not an end position. Do not change the String overloads.
items.why_local: A clear one-line bug: AOSP's signature is drawText(char[] text, int index, int count, ...), but the code passes count on as an end index.

items.title: IntentFilter.match discards the action-mismatch result
items.android_behavior: AOSP returns NO_MATCH_ACTION as soon as the action does not match, and a filter that declares data schemes does not match an intent with no data.
items.impact: Context.resolveActivityInternal (used from native to resolve incoming intents) scores every filter as a positive match when the intent has no data. Any activity with any intent-filter can be picked regardless of action, so the wrong activity opens.
items.suggested_fix: Return -3 right after the failed action check. When scheme==null and the filter has data schemes, return NO_MATCH_DATA. Check categories too.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/IntentFilter.java, method match(String action, String type, String scheme, Uri data, Set<String> categories, String logTag): replace `if (!matchAction(action)) { ret = -3; }` with `if (action != null && !matchAction(action)) { return -3 /*NO_MATCH_ACTION*/; }` so a mismatched action returns immediately (AOSP IntentFilter.match returns NO_MATCH_ACTION early, and a null action is not rejected). Keep the scheme logic below unchanged.
items.why_local: Confirmed: the NO_MATCH_ACTION result is overwritten by the scheme check, so resolveActivityInternal can pick an activity whose action does not match. The AOSP fix is a one-line early return.

items.title: AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator (the default for every ValueAnimator) and PathInterpolator are linear
items.android_behavior: AOSP: (float)(Math.cos((input + 1) * Math.PI) / 2.0f) + 0.5f. PathInterpolator evaluates the cubic bezier or path (e.g. 0.4,0,0.2,1 for fast-out-slow-in).
items.impact: Every ObjectAnimator/ValueAnimator without an explicit interpolator, and every framework PathInterpolator curve, moves linearly. Motion looks mechanical everywhere, though it does not break.
items.suggested_fix: Port the AOSP formula. For PathInterpolator, port the AOSP implementation (build a lookup table from the Path or cubic control points).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/animation/AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator.java, change getInterpolation(float input) to return the AOSP formula `(float)(Math.cos((input + 1) * Math.PI) / 2.0f) + 0.5f;`. Change nothing else; do not touch PathInterpolator in this task.
items.why_local: AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator is a one-line AOSP formula. PathInterpolator (cubic bezier) is harder and should be left out of this task, for Claude to do later.

items.title: attachViewToParent adds a view twice when it was not previously detached
items.android_behavior: AOSP attachViewToParent inserts the view into mChildren exactly once.
items.impact: If the view was not in detachedChildren (for example a RecyclerView view removed with removeDetachedView earlier and then re-attached, or a direct call), addViewInternal already inserts it into `children`, and the following children.add inserts it again. The child is then measured, laid out, hit-tested and iterated twice; getChildCount()/getChildAt() are off by one, which corrupts LayoutManager bookkeeping.
items.suggested_fix: Return right after addViewInternal(...) in the not-detached branch, or skip children.add when the view is already in the list.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/ViewGroup.java attachViewToParent(View view, int index, LayoutParams params): inside `if (!detachedChildren.remove(view)) { addViewInternal(view, index, params, false); }`, add `return;` right after the addViewInternal call. addViewInternal has already set the parent and layout params, added the view to children and called native_addView, so the rest of the method must run only for views that were really detached.
items.why_local: Confirmed: when the view was not detached, addViewInternal already adds it to children and to the native widget, and the code then adds it to children a second time. One early return fixes it.

items.title: Drawable caches' shouldInvalidateEntry throws, so Resources.updateConfiguration crashes after drawables are cached
items.android_behavior: AOSP returns Configuration.needNewResources(configChanges, entry.getChangingConfigurations()) and prunes only the affected entries.
items.impact: ThemedResourceCache.prune calls shouldInvalidateEntry on every live entry when configChanges != 0. Apps with an in-app language or font-size picker that call resources.updateConfiguration(config, metrics) (still widespread) get UnsupportedOperationException as soon as any drawable is cached.
items.suggested_fix: Implement both overrides as `return Configuration.needNewResources(configChanges, entry.getChangingConfigurations());` (as ConfigurationBoundResourceCache already does).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/res/Resources.java there are two anonymous `new ThemedResourceCache<Drawable.ConstantState>() { protected boolean shouldInvalidateEntry(...) }` blocks (fields mDrawableCacheInternal and mColorDrawableCache). In both, replace the `throw new UnsupportedOperationException(...)` and the TODO comment with `return Configuration.needNewResources(configChanges, entry.getChangingConfigurations());` (same as AOSP DrawableCache.shouldInvalidateEntry and ConfigurationBoundResourceCache.shouldInvalidateEntry in this repo).
items.why_local: Confirmed: both anonymous ThemedResourceCache subclasses throw from shouldInvalidateEntry, and prune() calls that method whenever configChanges != 0. AOSP DrawableCache has a one-line implementation, and ConfigurationBoundResourceCache in the same package already does the same thing.

items.title: ViewGroup.offsetChildrenTopAndBottom is an empty FIXME, but GridView depends on it
items.android_behavior: AOSP offsets every child's top and bottom by `offset` (child.offsetTopAndBottom). AbsListView/GridView use it to correct gaps after filling and to scroll.
items.impact: In GridView-based screens (galleries, launchers, icon pickers, older apps), the post-fill corrections (correctTooHigh/correctTooLow, adjustViewsUpOrDown) and keyboard/position scrolling do nothing. Rows overlap or leave gaps, and selection scrolling breaks.
items.suggested_fix: for (View child : children) child.offsetTopAndBottom(offset); then invalidate().
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/ViewGroup.java, replace the `// FIXME` body of offsetChildrenTopAndBottom(int offset) with a loop over all children: `for (int i = 0; i < getChildCount(); i++) getChildAt(i).offsetTopAndBottom(offset);`. AOSP moves every child vertically by offset pixels (mTop += offset, mBottom += offset). Do not change anything else.
items.why_local: Confirmed: the method is an empty FIXME. AOSP just shifts each child's top and bottom, and View.offsetTopAndBottom already exists, so the fix is a loop of a few lines.

items.title: TextView.setHint is empty and getHint() returns the literal "HINT"
items.android_behavior: Stores the hint and returns it. Apps and libraries (TextInputLayout, accessibility, empty-state logic) read getHint().
items.impact: Code that copies or compares the hint gets "HINT", and TextInputLayout-style floating labels can show "HINT". Plain TextViews never show the hint set in XML.
items.suggested_fix: Store the hint in a field, return it (null by default), and show it natively when the text is empty.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/widget/TextView.java: add a field private CharSequence hint = null;. setHint(CharSequence s) must set this.hint = s. getHint() must return hint (null when unset), not the literal "HINT". Leave setHint(int resId) as is (it already forwards). Do not modify EditText, which overrides both methods.
items.why_local: Storing and returning the hint is trivial and unambiguous (EditText already overrides both methods natively). Showing the hint on a plain TextView would need native work, but the stored value already fixes getHint.

items.title: openFileOutput ignores MODE_APPEND; fileList() always empty
items.android_behavior: AOSP opens with append=(mode & MODE_APPEND)!=0 in getFilesDir() (creating it), and fileList() lists getFilesDir().
items.impact: Apps that append logs, history or journals with MODE_APPEND truncate the file on every write and lose data. The files dir is not created first, so the first write can throw FileNotFoundException. Apps enumerating saved files with fileList() see none.
items.suggested_fix: return new FileOutputStream(new File(getFilesDir(), name), (mode & 0x8000) != 0); and fileList(): String[] l = getFilesDir().list(); return l != null ? l : new String[0];
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/content/Context.java: (1) In openFileOutput(String name, int mode), replace the return statement with `return new FileOutputStream(new File(getFilesDir(), name), (mode & 0x8000) != 0);` (0x8000 is Context.MODE_APPEND in AOSP; use the constant if the class defines it). (2) In fileList(), return the names of the files in getFilesDir(): `String[] list = getFilesDir().list(); return list != null ? list : new String[0];` (AOSP ContextImpl.fileList does this).
items.why_local: Confirmed: openFileOutput builds its path by hand and ignores MODE_APPEND, and fileList() always returns empty. The fix is a small Java change using the existing getFilesDir(), which points at the same directory.

items.title: getSuggestedMinimumWidth/Height ignore the background drawable's minimum size
items.android_behavior: AOSP: (mBackground == null) ? mMinHeight : max(mMinHeight, mBackground.getMinimumHeight()), and the same for width.
items.impact: Custom views (and View/ImageView-like widgets using the default onMeasure) with a 9-patch or sized shape background measure to 0 or too small under wrap_content: dividers, progress tracks and badges collapse or are clipped.
items.suggested_fix: Include background.getMinimumWidth()/getMinimumHeight() as AOSP does.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/View.java: getSuggestedMinimumHeight() returns `(background == null) ? getMinimumHeight() : Math.max(getMinimumHeight(), background.getMinimumHeight());`. getSuggestedMinimumWidth() returns the same with widths. This is the AOSP implementation. Keep the @Export annotations.
items.why_local: AOSP behaviour is a single expression and Drawable.getMinimumWidth/Height exist. It can change measured sizes where backgrounds report a minimum size, but that is the correct AOSP result.

items.title: DateFormat.getDateFormat returns a date+time SimpleDateFormat; getDateFormatString is hard-coded to "dd. MM. yyyy"
items.android_behavior: getDateFormat returns the locale's short date-only format (java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(SHORT)). getDateFormatOrder follows the locale.
items.impact: Apps formatting dates with DateFormat.getDateFormat(ctx) show '11/21/26, 12:34 PM' (with time) in date-only columns such as notes, file lists and transaction lists. getDateFormatOrder always reports the Czech/Slovak day-month-year order regardless of locale, which misorders date pickers.
items.suggested_fix: Return java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(java.text.DateFormat.SHORT) and derive getDateFormatString from that instance's toPattern() for the current locale.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/text/format/DateFormat.java: make `getDateFormat(Context context)` return `java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(java.text.DateFormat.SHORT)` (date only, current locale, as AOSP does when no user setting exists). Make the private `getDateFormatString(Context context)` return `((java.text.SimpleDateFormat) java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(java.text.DateFormat.SHORT)).toPattern()` instead of the hard-coded "dd. MM. yyyy", so getDateFormatOrder follows the locale. Do not touch the commented-out getDateFormatForSetting block.
items.why_local: A two-method, Java-only change in one file with clear AOSP semantics: a locale SHORT date format and its pattern.

items.title: unscheduleDrawable is a no-op, so animated drawables cannot be stopped
items.android_behavior: AOSP removes the posted callbacks (Choreographer/handler removeCallbacks(what, who)), so AnimationDrawable.stop(), AnimatedVectorDrawable/ProgressBar stop and setVisible(false) halt the animation.
items.impact: Frame animations (AnimationDrawable loading spinners, animated icons) keep running after stop() or after the view is hidden or detached. They burn CPU, keep invalidating, and may resume visually after the app stopped them.
items.suggested_fix: getHandler().removeCallbacks(runnable) for the two-argument form; for the one-argument form, removeCallbacksAndMessages(drawable) after posting with the drawable as token (postAtTime(runnable, drawable, when)).
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/View.java: scheduleDrawable(Drawable drawable, Runnable runnable, long time) becomes `getHandler().postAtTime(runnable, drawable, time);` (time is already in uptimeMillis; the drawable is the token). unscheduleDrawable(Drawable drawable, Runnable runnable) becomes `getHandler().removeCallbacks(runnable, drawable);`. unscheduleDrawable(Drawable drawable) becomes `getHandler().removeCallbacksAndMessages(drawable);`. This matches AOSP, which posts and removes drawable callbacks keyed by the drawable.
items.why_local: Confirmed: both unscheduleDrawable overloads are empty. Handler already has postAtTime(Runnable, Object token, long), removeCallbacks(Runnable, Object) and removeCallbacksAndMessages(Object), so the fix is three one-line bodies.

items.title: getClipToPadding()/getClipChildren() return false; AOSP defaults are true and the setters are no-ops
items.android_behavior: AOSP defaults both flags to true, reads them from android:clipToPadding/clipChildren, and the getters reflect the setters.
items.impact: Code that branches on getClipToPadding() (LayoutManagers in custom lists, ViewPager/indicator libraries, SwipeRefreshLayout offsets) behaves as if clipToPadding=false was requested on every container, which leads to off-by-padding positioning and scroll limits.
items.suggested_fix: Store both flags (default true), read the XML attrs, and return the stored values, even if clipping itself is still handled by GTK.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/view/ViewGroup.java: add fields `private boolean clipToPadding = true;` and `private boolean clipChildren = true;` (AOSP defaults). setClipToPadding(b) stores into clipToPadding, and getClipToPadding() returns it. setClipChildren(b) stores into clipChildren, and getClipChildren() returns it. Do not add any rendering or native calls.
items.why_local: Clipping is not implemented, but backing the getters with fields that default to true and are written by the setters matches AOSP getter behaviour. It is trivial, and RecyclerView already overrides clipToPadding itself.

items.title: VectorDrawable ignores android:fillType, so evenOdd paths are filled with the nonzero rule
items.android_behavior: <path android:fillType="evenOdd"> (API 24+, emitted by Android Studio's SVG importer for many icons) fills with the even-odd rule, so inner contours become holes.
items.impact: Icons converted from SVG with evenOdd (rings, donuts, letter counters like 'o' and 'e', outlined shapes) render with their holes filled in, giving solid blobs in toolbars, buttons and empty-state illustrations.
items.suggested_fix: Read VectorDrawablePath_fillType (0 = nonZero, 1 = evenOdd) into VFullPath, and call path.setFillType(EVEN_ODD) on the render path before drawing that path.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/drawable/VectorDrawable.java, class VFullPath (around line 2121): add a field 'int mFillType = 0;' (AOSP: 0 = nonZero/WINDING, 1 = evenOdd/EVEN_ODD), copy it in the VFullPath copy constructor next to mStrokeMiterlimit ('mFillType = copy.mFillType;'), and in VFullPath.updateStateFromTypedArray read 'mFillType = a.getInt(R.styleable.VectorDrawablePath_fillType, mFillType);'. In the renderer's drawPath (around line 1728), just before 'canvas.drawPath(mRenderPath, fillPaint);', call 'mRenderPath.setFillType(fullPath.mFillType == 0 ? Path.FillType.WINDING : Path.FillType.EVEN_ODD);'. Do not change stroke drawing.
items.why_local: Native drawPath already honours Path.FillType (fill_rule is passed down). Only the VectorDrawable attribute parsing and a setFillType call before the fill draw are missing.

items.title: ThumbnailUtils.extractThumbnail stretches instead of centre-cropping
items.evidence: A few lines using the existing createScaledBitmap and createBitmap(src,x,y,w,h). AOSP behaviour (scale to cover, then centre crop) is clear.
items.fix_hint: extractThumbnail(source, width, height): if source == null return null; float scale = Math.max((float)width / source.getWidth(), (float)height / source.getHeight()); int sw = Math.max(width, Math.round(source.getWidth() * scale)), sh = Math.max(height, Math.round(source.getHeight() * scale)); Bitmap scaled = Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(source, sw, sh, true); return Bitmap.createBitmap(scaled, (sw - width) / 2, (sh - height) / 2, width, height). Add the overload extractThumbnail(Bitmap, int, int, int options) delegating to it (OPTIONS_RECYCLE_INPUT=2: recycle source when set and source != result).
items.why_local: A few lines using the existing createScaledBitmap and createBitmap(src,x,y,w,h). AOSP behaviour (scale to cover, then centre crop) is clear.

items.title: Ringtone.getTitle returns a visible placeholder string; RingtoneManager.getDefaultUri returns an empty Uri
items.android_behavior: getTitle returns the ringtone's display name (or 'Default (X)' / 'Silent'). getDefaultUri returns Settings.System.DEFAULT_RINGTONE_URI, DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI or DEFAULT_ALARM_ALERT_URI.
items.impact: Alarm, timer, reminder and messaging apps show 'FIXME: Ringtone.getTitle()' in their settings UI. The empty default Uri, stored as the chosen sound or passed to MediaPlayer or a NotificationChannel, yields silent alerts.
items.suggested_fix: Return the last path segment or a 'Default' label for settings URIs. Have getDefaultUri return Settings.System.DEFAULT_RINGTONE_URI/DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI (and an alarm URI) by type.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/media/RingtoneManager.java add the AOSP constants TYPE_RINGTONE=1, TYPE_NOTIFICATION=2, TYPE_ALARM=4 if they are missing. Make getDefaultUri(int type) return Settings.System.DEFAULT_RINGTONE_URI for TYPE_RINGTONE, Settings.System.DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI for TYPE_NOTIFICATION, Settings.System.DEFAULT_ALARM_ALERT_URI for TYPE_ALARM, and null otherwise. Add `public static final Uri DEFAULT_ALARM_ALERT_URI = getUriFor("alarm_alert");` to Settings.System next to the other two if it is missing. In src/api-impl/android/media/Ringtone.java make getTitle(Context) return "Default ringtone" instead of the FIXME placeholder (AOSP shows a generic title when no media title is known).
items.why_local: Low impact. Clear AOSP mapping from type to the Settings.System default URIs, plus a non-placeholder title, in two or three small Java files.

items.title: Context.deleteFile(String) and android.util.LogPrinter missing
items.evidence: Two trivial, well-specified AOSP APIs from corpus missing_api hits: io.homeassistant minimal (deleteFile, BLANK) and com.vermont.possin (LogPrinter, BLANK).

New LogPrinter implements Printer: fields int priority, String tag, int buffer; constructor LogPrinter(int priority, String tag) sets buffer = Log.LOG_ID_MAIN if that exists, else 0; println(String x) calls Log.println(priority, tag, x).
