items.title: InputFilter.LengthFilter.filter always returns "" (delete) instead of null (accept), and has no max
items.android_behavior: LengthFilter keeps max and returns null (keep input) when the result fits, or the trimmed prefix otherwise. getMax() returns max.
items.impact: TextView.setFilters is currently a no-op, so this is latent in widgets. However, apps and libraries that call filters manually (input validators, chat composers, AndroidX EmojiCompat and Material text field counters) treat every keystroke as rejected, and text is erased. Wiring setFilters up later will block all typing in fields with android:maxLength.
items.suggested_fix: Port AOSP LengthFilter: store mMax, keep = mMax - (dest.length() - (dend - dstart)), return null/""/subSequence accordingly, and add getMax().
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/text/InputFilter.java LengthFilter: add `private final int mMax;`, set it in the constructor, add `public int getMax() { return mMax; }`, and implement filter() exactly as AOSP does: `int keep = mMax - (dest.length() - (dend - dstart)); if (keep <= 0) return ""; else if (keep >= end - start) return null; else { keep += start; if (Character.isHighSurrogate(source.charAt(keep - 1))) { --keep; if (keep == start) return ""; } return source.subSequence(start, keep); }`. Returning null means accept the input unchanged.
items.why_local: The AOSP LengthFilter code is short and well known. One file, verifiable by reading the diff. Impact is low because TextView.setFilters is currently a no-op.

items.title: android.view.animation.BounceInterpolator missing (ClassNotFoundException crash)
items.evidence: A pure-math class with a well-known AOSP formula, copying the pattern of the existing OvershootInterpolator/CycleInterpolator. Found in mg-microg (indi.dmzz_yyhyy.lightnovelreader CRASH).
items.fix_hint: public class BounceInterpolator extends BaseInterpolator { public BounceInterpolator() {} public BounceInterpolator(Context c, AttributeSet a) {} private static float bounce(float t) { return t * t * 8.0f; } public float getInterpolation(float t) { t *= 1.1226f; if (t < 0.3535f) return bounce(t); else if (t < 0.7408f) return bounce(t - 0.54719f) + 0.7f; else if (t < 0.9644f) return bounce(t - 0.8526f) + 0.9f; else return bounce(t - 1.0435f) + 0.95f; } }. Match the constructor signatures of the neighbouring interpolators.
items.why_local: A pure-math class with a well-known AOSP formula, copying the pattern of the existing OvershootInterpolator/CycleInterpolator. Found in mg-microg (indi.dmzz_yyhyy.lightnovelreader CRASH).

items.title: LayerDrawable.setColorFilter is commented out and setTintList is missing, so layer-list and ripple tints are ignored
items.android_behavior: LayerDrawable passes setColorFilter, setTintList and setTintBlendMode on to every layer.
items.impact: View.setBackgroundTintList / app:backgroundTint and DrawableCompat.setTint on layer-list or ripple backgrounds (AppCompat/Material buttons, FABs, chips) silently keep the original colours. Coloured buttons appear in the default grey or accent colour.

items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/graphics/drawable/LayerDrawable.java, uncomment the setColorFilter(ColorFilter cf) override (around line 431) and add '@Override' to it. Add two overrides in the same style, as in AOSP LayerDrawable: 'public void setTintList(ColorStateList tint)' and 'public void setTintMode(PorterDuff.Mode tintMode)'. Each loops i from 0 to mLayerState.mNum-1 over mLayerState.mChildren and calls the same method on array[i].mDrawable, skipping a child whose mDrawable is null. Add the null check to setColorFilter as well. Add imports android.content.res.ColorStateList and android.graphics.PorterDuff if missing (ColorFilter is already imported). No other changes.

items.title: Canvas.drawPoint, drawARGB and drawColor(int, PorterDuff.Mode) are logging stubs; drawPoints treats offset/count as points
items.evidence: One Java file that delegates to existing drawRect, drawCircle and drawColor. The AOSP semantics are clear from the javadoc: drawPoint paints a square or round dot of strokeWidth (hairline = 1px), and drawPoints' offset and count are in floats.
items.fix_hint: drawPoint(x,y,paint): Paint p = new Paint(paint); p.setStyle(Paint.Style.FILL); float h = Math.max(paint.getStrokeWidth(), 1f) / 2; if (paint.getStrokeCap() == Paint.Cap.ROUND) drawCircle(x, y, h, p); else drawRect(x - h, y - h, x + h, y + h, p). drawPoints(pts, paint) calls drawPoints(pts, 0, pts.length, paint). drawPoints(pts, offset, count, paint): for (int i = offset; i + 1 < offset + count; i += 2) drawPoint(pts[i], pts[i + 1], paint). drawARGB(a,r,g,b) calls drawColor(Color.argb(a, r, g, b)). drawColor(color, mode): if mode == PorterDuff.Mode.SRC_OVER, or (mode == SRC && Color.alpha(color) == 255), call drawColor(color); otherwise keep the warning (CLEAR/other modes need real compositing).
items.why_local: One Java file that delegates to existing drawRect, drawCircle and drawColor. The AOSP semantics are clear from the javadoc: drawPoint paints a square or round dot of strokeWidth (hairline = 1px), and drawPoints' offset and count are in floats.

items.title: Toast: no setText/setDuration/getDuration, cancel() does nothing, duration ignored

Add setText(CharSequence) and setText(int resId) (mContext.getString), setDuration(int)/getDuration(), getView() returning null. In show(), store the notification id in a field and use a delay of duration == LENGTH_LONG ? 3500 : 2000. cancel(): if shown, ((NotificationManager)mContext.getSystemService("notification")).cancel(id) and remove the pending Handler callback (keep the Handler and Runnable in fields).

items.title: WebViewClient callbacks use non-AOSP signatures: onPageStarted(WebView,String) and only the String shouldOverrideUrlLoading are called, so app overrides never run
items.android_behavior: The real signature is onPageStarted(WebView, String, Bitmap favicon). Since API 24 the framework calls shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, WebResourceRequest), whose default implementation delegates to the String version. Apps override the 3-arg onPageStarted and the WebResourceRequest variant.
items.impact: App overrides of onPageStarted(view, url, favicon) are never called (progress bars never show, URL bars never update). Apps that only override shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, WebResourceRequest), the modern default, never see navigations. OAuth login flows that capture the redirect URI there (Mastodon/Lemmy/Matrix and other clients) hang on the redirect page, and 'open links externally' logic fails.
items.suggested_fix: Add onPageStarted(WebView,String,Bitmap) and call it with a null favicon. Add shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, WebResourceRequest) whose default delegates to the String version, and have native call the WebResourceRequest variant with a simple WebResourceRequest implementation. Add onReceivedError/shouldInterceptRequest stubs with AOSP signatures.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/webkit/WebViewClient.java add the AOSP signatures: `public void onPageStarted(WebView view, String url, android.graphics.Bitmap favicon) {}` and `public boolean shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView view, WebResourceRequest request) { return shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view, request.getUrl().toString()); }` (the AOSP default delegates to the deprecated String version). Keep the existing String shouldOverrideUrlLoading (AOSP has it, deprecated). The 2-arg onPageStarted is not AOSP: keep it only if something else calls it. In src/api-impl/android/webkit/WebView.java: internalLoadChanged must call `webViewClient.onPageStarted(this, url, null)`. internalShouldOverrideUrlLoading must build a WebResourceRequest (an anonymous class implementing the interface: getUrl() -> Uri.parse(url), isForMainFrame() -> true, isRedirect() -> false, hasGesture() -> false, getMethod() -> "GET", getRequestHeaders() -> empty map) and call `webViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading(this, request)`. Do not change the @Export methods' own signatures (native code calls them).
items.why_local: Java-only, two files (WebViewClient.java, WebView.java), with well-documented AOSP signatures. The reviewer can check the delegation chain from the diff alone. Fossify apps rarely use WebView, so impact is low.

items.title: View.dispatchApplyWindowInsets missing, setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener is a no-op and its interface has no method; WindowInsets.getInsetsIgnoringVisibility missing
items.evidence: Java only, with AOSP dispatch semantics that are short and clear. Corpus hits: pinpoi (NoSuchMethodError dispatchApplyWindowInsets, BLANK) and roamingguard (getInsetsIgnoringVisibility, BLANK). ATL has no system bars, so the insets stay zero and only the call plumbing is needed.
items.fix_hint: View: the interface OnApplyWindowInsetsListener gets the method WindowInsets onApplyWindowInsets(View v, WindowInsets insets). Store the listener in setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener. Add public WindowInsets dispatchApplyWindowInsets(WindowInsets insets) { return listener != null ? listener.onApplyWindowInsets(this, insets) : onApplyWindowInsets(insets); }. Add requestApplyInsets() if missing (no-op is fine). ViewGroup: override dispatchApplyWindowInsets to call super, then, unless the result isConsumed(), call child.dispatchApplyWindowInsets(insets) for each child. WindowInsets: add public Insets getInsetsIgnoringVisibility(int typeMask) { return getInsets(typeMask); }.

items.title: TextUtils.htmlEncode returns its input unescaped; TextUtils.ellipsize never truncates
items.android_behavior: htmlEncode escapes < > & ' ". ellipsize measures with the paint and returns a truncated copy with an ellipsis at START/MIDDLE/END.
items.impact: Apps that build HTML for Html.fromHtml, WebView.loadData or TextView embed user text unescaped. That can break the markup (and, combined with Pango markup mode, blank the label) or inject HTML. Custom views and adapters that ellipsize titles to fit a width draw overflowing, overlapping text.
items.suggested_fix: Port AOSP htmlEncode (a switch over the five characters). Implement ellipsize using Paint.measureText/breakText, or a Pango layout with ellipsize and width.
items.fix_hint: In src/api-impl/android/text/TextUtils.java: (1) htmlEncode(String s): build a StringBuilder, replacing '<' with "<", '>' with ">", '&' with "&", '\'' with "'" (AOSP uses ') and '"' with """, and copying every other char unchanged. (2) ellipsize(CharSequence text, TextPaint p, float avail, TruncateAt where): if `p.measureText(text, 0, text.length()) <= avail` return text unchanged. Otherwise, with ellipsis "…": for END (and MARQUEE), find the longest prefix such that measureText(prefix + ellipsis) <= avail and return prefix + ellipsis. For START, return ellipsis + the longest fitting suffix. For MIDDLE, keep a prefix and a suffix of about equal length around the ellipsis. If not even the ellipsis fits, return "". Use a simple loop that shrinks the kept length; do not add new native code.
items.why_local: Both methods are small and pure Java with clear AOSP semantics. htmlEncode is trivial. ellipsize can loop over Paint.measureText, which is only approximate in ATL, but the code is still correct by inspection.

items.title: NotificationChannel stores nothing and has no getters; getNotificationChannel(s) return null/empty; cancelAll is a no-op
items.evidence: Data class plus bookkeeping in two Java files, with no native change: cancelAll reuses cancel(id). Apps that read back their channel (importance checks, 'notifications disabled' prompts) get null today, and any getter call on a channel would be a NoSuchMethodError.
items.fix_hint: NotificationChannel: store id, name, importance, description, group, showBadge, lockscreenVisibility, lightColor, lights, vibrationPattern, vibration, sound and audioAttributes from the constructor and setters. Add getId, getName, getImportance, setImportance, getDescription, setDescription, getGroup, canShowBadge, getLockscreenVisibility, getLightColor, shouldShowLights, getVibrationPattern, shouldVibrate, getSound, getAudioAttributes, setName. NotificationManager: static LinkedHashMap<String,NotificationChannel> channels. createNotificationChannel puts it unless the id already exists (AOSP keeps the user's importance; only update name and description). createNotificationChannels loops. getNotificationChannel(id) returns map.get(id). getNotificationChannels returns new ArrayList<>(values). deleteNotificationChannel removes it. Track a static Set<Integer> of active ids (add in notify for non-MediaStyle, remove in cancel); cancelAll() calls cancel(id) for a copy of the set.
